For efficient panning of input channels to fixed locations in the output, use the pans attribute. The attribute values specify the panning location for each input channel within the output channel space. Refer to the circular and linear panning tabs for more information. pans works with any setting of the pancontrolmode attribute; the default (used below) is normalized circular panning

observe that @activechans does not change the number of outputs in the mc.mixdown~ multichannel patch cord
additional channels will be zero if @activechans is less than the total number of outputs
@autogain will scale by @activechans as it changes

mc.mixdown~ can dynamically and temporarily reduce the number of output channels using the @activechans attribute. This can be useful if you want to hear your mix with different output channel counts (or if someone stole a few of your speakers!). Remember that @activechans can only reduce the total channel count supplied as argument to mc.mixdown~ so make the channel count value as large as you might need.
mc.mixdown~ uses several attributes that let you customize how the gain of inputs and panning is scaled

autogain scaling factor is 2 (outputs) over 4 (inputs) equals 0.5

By default, when a pan signal input is connected, mc.mixdown~ applies a √2 / 2 scaling factor to the input as part of its constant power panning algorithm. If you do not want this scaling factor applied, enable the @linearpanmode attribute.

By default, mc.mixdown~ does not scale the output when it is mixed. However, as more input signals are mixed the output will increase in level, so if you want to maintain a consistent maximum output level regardless of input channel count, you can enable the @autogain attribute. @autogain adds a scaling factor to the output equal to the output channel count divided by the input channel count.

The linear mc.mixdown~ pan control modes (@pancontrolmode 1 and 2) use a linear arrangement where panning all the way to the lowest-numbered channel is at 0 and panning all the way to the highest numbered channel is at 1. With @pancontrolmode 2, you can use whole numbers (1 - N) to focus the panning on specific channels. Unlike the circular pan mode, with the linear pan mode there is no way to pan a signal between the first and last channel. For stereo (e.g., mc.stereo~) this doesn't matter but it may be a concern for higher output channel counts.
using a single-channel signal pans all inputs identically
You can also set the @pancontrolmode to 3 to use whole numbers to refer to the channels

The default mc.mixdown~ pan mode (@pancontrolmode 0) is a circle where 0.5 is in the front middle and 0 and 1 are in the rear middle. All speakers are evenly spaced around the circle based on the number of output channels.
